_readme: Rotating hero quotes. Words of OTHERS only, never the site author. Every entry must be verbatim from a public, filed, or public-domain source and must name where in the published work it appears (cited_in). Validated at build by scripts/validate-quotes.mjs. Lives in src/data (not content/) because vite.config special-cases content/*.json for the CMS loader. Submissions arrive through midesk/.claude/agent_notes/_shared/20260905_hero_quotes_submissions.md; website-developer wires them in.

quotes.text: There is great reason that the King himself shall take account of it, and no other.
quotes.attribution: Sir Edward Coke
quotes.source: Floyd v. Barker (Star Chamber, 1607), 12 Co. Rep. 23, 77 Eng. Rep. 1307
quotes.cited_in: Plaintiff's Opposition to the Federal Defendants' Motion to Dismiss, Doc 73 ¶ 87

quotes.text: Shall not be drawn in question before any other Judge, for any surmise of corruption, except before the King himself.
quotes.attribution: Sir Edward Coke
quotes.source: Floyd v. Barker (Star Chamber, 1607), 12 Co. Rep. 23, 77 Eng. Rep. 1307
quotes.cited_in: Plaintiff's Opposition to the Federal Defendants' Motion to Dismiss, Doc 73 ¶ 87

quotes.text: It's the Birthright of the Subject to Petition.
quotes.attribution: Mr. Justice Holloway, King's Bench
quotes.source: The Trial of the Seven Bishops (King's Bench, 1688), 1739 print, p. 413
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Seven Bishops trial (1688), read at the 1739 print (forthcoming)

quotes.text: To make it a Libel it must be False, it must be Malicious, and it must tend to Sedition.
quotes.attribution: Mr. Justice Powell, King's Bench
quotes.source: The Trial of the Seven Bishops (King's Bench, 1688), 1739 print, p. 422
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Seven Bishops trial (1688), read at the 1739 print (forthcoming)

quotes.text: If this be once allowed of, there will need no Parliament, all the Legislature will be in the King.
quotes.attribution: Mr. Justice Powell, King's Bench
quotes.source: The Trial of the Seven Bishops (King's Bench, 1688), 1739 print, p. 424
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Seven Bishops trial (1688), read at the 1739 print (forthcoming)

quotes.text: Access to the sovereign must not be shut up in case of the subjects distresses.
quotes.attribution: The Court of Star Chamber, resolution of the whole Court
quotes.source: Wrenham's Case (Star Chamber, 1618), Hobart 220, 80 Eng. Rep. 367
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Coke–Bacon rivalry and the Star Chamber institution (forthcoming)

quotes.text: In causa sua propria nemo potest esse Judex.
quotes.attribution: William Lyndwood, gloss on Stephen Langton's constitution (Oxford, 1222)
quotes.source: Provinciale (Oxford, 1679), p. 312, gloss r. 'In his own cause no man can be judge.'
quotes.cited_in: Research library: Roman, canon and biblical sources of the Floyd rule (forthcoming)

quotes.text: So long as he is the true minister of God, and pronounceth according to his worde.
quotes.attribution: The Geneva Bible's annotators, note on Deuteronomy 17:12
quotes.source: The Bible and Holy Scriptures (Geneva, 1560), fol. 88v, original spelling
quotes.cited_in: Research library: Roman, canon and biblical sources of the Floyd rule (forthcoming)

quotes.text: Ut poena ad paucos, metus ad omnes perveniat, without respect of persons, be they publique or private, great or small.
quotes.attribution: Sir Edward Coke
quotes.source: The Fourth Part of the Institutes of the Laws of England, cap. 5, The Court of Star-Chamber, p. 63 (London, 1797 ed.)
quotes.cited_in: Research library: a restorative and comparative history of sovereign, absolute and qualified immunity (book manuscript, forthcoming)

quotes.text: Geue no sentence before thou hast herde the cause, but first let men tell out their tayles.
quotes.attribution: Ecclesiasticus 11:8, Coverdale Bible
quotes.source: Biblia, the Bible (Myles Coverdale, 1535), Ecclus. xi, fo. xlij
quotes.cited_in: Research library: a restorative and comparative history of sovereign, absolute and qualified immunity (book manuscript, forthcoming)

quotes.text: Go not to lawe with the iudge: for he wyll iudge accordynge to hys awne honoure.
quotes.attribution: Ecclesiasticus 8:14, Great Bible
quotes.source: The Byble in Englyshe (Great Bible, Cranmer ed., 1540), Jesus the sonne of Syrach, fo. xxxix
quotes.cited_in: Research library: a restorative and comparative history of sovereign, absolute and qualified immunity (book manuscript, forthcoming)

quotes.text: Heare the small as well as the greate, and be afrayed of no man, for the iudgement is Gods.
quotes.attribution: Deuteronomy 1:17, Great Bible
quotes.source: The Byble in Englyshe (Great Bible, 1540), Deuteronomium, chapter 1
quotes.cited_in: Research library: a restorative and comparative history of sovereign, absolute and qualified immunity (book manuscript, forthcoming)

quotes.text: Questions which merely lurk in the record, neither brought to the attention of the court nor ruled upon, are not to be considered as having been so decided as to constitute precedents.
quotes.attribution: Justice George Sutherland, for the Court
quotes.source: Webster v. Fall, 266 U.S. 507, 511 (1925)
quotes.cited_in: Plaintiff's Opposition to the Federal Defendants' Motion to Dismiss, Doc 73 ¶ 94

quotes.text: a reversion to the old notion that the King can do no wrong
quotes.attribution: Justice Byron White, dissenting for four Justices
quotes.source: Nixon v. Fitzgerald, 457 U.S. 731, 766 (1982)
quotes.cited_in: Plaintiff's Opposition to the Federal Defendants' Motion to Dismiss, Doc 73 ¶ 91

quotes.text: the instructions cannot change the nature of the transaction, or legalize an act which without those instructions would have been a plain trespass
quotes.attribution: Chief Justice John Marshall
quotes.source: Little v. Barreme, 6 U.S. (2 Cranch) 170, 179 (1804)
quotes.cited_in: Memorandum of Law B, Kirchner v. Ellison, D. Minn. No. 0:26-cv-00726, Doc. 26-14 ¶ 66

quotes.text: For protecting them, by a mock Trial, from punishment for any Murders which they should commit on the Inhabitants of these States
quotes.attribution: The Declaration of Independence (1776), list of grievances
quotes.source: Engrossed text, National Archives transcription
quotes.cited_in: Plaintiff's Opposition to the Federal Defendants' Motion to Dismiss, Doc 73 ¶ 93

quotes.text: serra prise del fyle et cancell et ousterment deface
quotes.attribution: Sir Edward Coke, in his own notebook of Floyd v. Barker. Law French: be taken off the file, cancelled, and utterly defaced
quotes.source: Reports from the Notebooks of Edward Coke, vol. VII, 142 Selden Soc. 1655–58 (Sir John Baker ed., 2025), as reproduced in the filed appendix
quotes.cited_in: Doc 73 ¶ 85; Documentary Appendix, Doc 73-1 at 48–55

quotes.text: No man in this country is so high that he is above the law.
quotes.attribution: Justice Samuel Miller, for the Court
quotes.source: United States v. Lee, 106 U.S. 196, 220 (1882)
quotes.cited_in: Plaintiff's Opposition to the Federal Defendants' Motion to Dismiss, Doc 73 ¶ 93

quotes.text: if this might bee suffered ye ground of all Justice would bee overthrowne
quotes.attribution: The Court of Star Chamber, giving the reason of its judgment in Floyd v. Barker, as reported by the anonymous manuscript reporter
quotes.source: Harvard Law School Library, HLS MS 149, f. 83r, ll. 19–21 (transcription, long s normalised)
quotes.cited_in: Doc 73 ¶ 86; archive leaf f. 83r

quotes.text: to remayne close prisoner vntill hee shall have confessed his abettors
quotes.attribution: The Star Chamber's sentence on Rice ap Evan Lloyd for accusing the judge, as reported (1607)
quotes.source: Harvard Law School Library, HLS MS 149, f. 83r, ll. 11–12 (transcription, long s normalised)
quotes.cited_in: Doc 73 ¶ 86; archive leaf f. 83r

quotes.text: The Jury asked forgivenes of William Aprice for the verdict / Aprice notwithstanding was condemned and executed
quotes.attribution: Anonymous law reporter, HLS MS 149, on the Anglesey murder trial behind Floyd v. Barker
quotes.source: Harvard Law School Library, HLS MS 149, f. 82r, ll. 12–15 (transcription; the virgule is the leaf's own paragraph mark)
quotes.cited_in: Doc 73 ¶¶ 84–85; archive leaf f. 82r

quotes.text: The witnesses not capable of the English Tongue vttered their deposicons in welsh but written in Englishe contrary to their sayings in welsh
quotes.attribution: Anonymous law reporter, HLS MS 149, on how the Welsh witnesses' evidence was recorded
quotes.source: Harvard Law School Library, HLS MS 149, f. 81v, ll. 5–8 (transcription, long s normalised)
quotes.cited_in: Doc 73 ¶ 85; archive leaf f. 81v

quotes.text: he was as innocent of the faulte whereof he was condemned as the childe new borne
quotes.attribution: William ap Rees ap William, condemned at Beaumaris, as deposed by his kinsman Rees ap Jevan Lloyd, prisoner in the Fleet (Star Chamber, June 1607)
quotes.source: The National Archives, STAC 8/203/38, m. 4, ll. 29–31 (transcription, expansions printed plain)
quotes.cited_in: Archive leaf m. 004

quotes.text: I praie you make knowne to the state after I am dead as you are my kinsman
quotes.attribution: William ap Rees ap William's dying charge to his kinsman, deposed by Rees ap Jevan Lloyd (Star Chamber, June 1607)
quotes.source: The National Archives, STAC 8/203/38, m. 4, ll. 35–37 (transcription)
quotes.cited_in: Archive leaf m. 004

quotes.text: Let them be Lions, but yet Lions vnder the Throne; Being circumspect, that they doe not checke, or oppose any Points of Soueraigntie.
quotes.attribution: Sir Francis Bacon, Viscount St Alban
quotes.source: The Essayes or Counsels, Civill and Morall (London, 1625), LVI, Of Iudicature, p. 324 (1625 spelling)
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Coke–Bacon rivalry and the Star Chamber institution (forthcoming)

quotes.text: Hereafter the Greatness of a Judge or Magistrate shall be no Sanctuary or Protection to him against Guiltiness.
quotes.attribution: Sir Francis Bacon, Lord Chancellor, in his submission to the House of Lords, 1621
quotes.source: A Collection of the Proceedings in the House of Commons against the Lord Verulam (2nd ed., London, 1721), p. 27
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Coke–Bacon rivalry and the 1621 proceedings against Lord Verulam (forthcoming)

quotes.text: The questioning of Men in eminent Places, hath the same Terror, though not the same Rigour with the Punishment.
quotes.attribution: Sir Francis Bacon, Lord Chancellor, to the House of Lords, 1621
quotes.source: A Collection of the Proceedings in the House of Commons against the Lord Verulam (2nd ed., London, 1721), p. 30
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Coke–Bacon rivalry and the 1621 proceedings against Lord Verulam (forthcoming)

quotes.text: You will make Bribery to be unpunish'd, if he who carrieth the Bribe shall not be a Witness.
quotes.attribution: Sir Edward Coke, in the House of Commons, 17 March 1621
quotes.source: A Collection of the Proceedings in the House of Commons against the Lord Verulam (2nd ed., London, 1721), p. 16
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Coke–Bacon rivalry and the 1621 proceedings against Lord Verulam (forthcoming)

quotes.text: If the Fountains be muddy, what will the Streams be? If the great Dispenser of the King's Conscience be corrupt, who can have any Courage to plead before him?
quotes.attribution: Sir Robert Philips, reporting to the House of Commons, 17 March 1621
quotes.source: A Collection of the Proceedings in the House of Commons against the Lord Verulam (2nd ed., London, 1721), pp. 11–12
quotes.cited_in: Research library: the Coke–Bacon rivalry and the 1621 proceedings against Lord Verulam (forthcoming)
